subject: english-language
title: Nouns and Verbs in Depth
welcome_lead: Go deeper than 'naming words' and 'doing words'.
meta_desc: KS3 English Language adventure on proper/common nouns and transitive verbs.
final_note: You can now classify nouns and verbs with finer detail.

walkthroughs.body_html: Proper nouns ('London', 'Sara') always take a capital. Common nouns ('city', 'girl') don't, unless they start a sentence.
Abstract nouns name ideas ('love', 'fear'). Concrete nouns name physical things ('chair', 'sand').
A transitive verb takes a direct object: 'She kicked the ball.' An intransitive verb doesn't: 'She arrived.'

mcqs.q: What is convergence in accommodation theory?
options: The IPA stands for International Phonetic Acronym.
When a speaker adjusts their speech to be more similar to their interlocutor's — to express solidarity, gain approval or ease communication.
Convergence is when two speakers start using identical accents permanently.
Convergence means two languages merge into one new language.

mcqs.q: What is the IPA in linguistics?
options: The International Phonetic Alphabet — a standardised set of symbols where each symbol represents one distinct sound. Used to transcribe pronunciation precisely across all languages.
The IPA stands for International Phonetic Acronym.
The IPA is just another alphabet like the Roman or Greek alphabet.
Convergence means two languages merge into one new language.
